subject: Federation attribute mapping, SCIM throttling, and admin SLA discussion
messages:
From: Sarah Bates <sarah.bates@medipharm.com>

Date: Wed, 30 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SSO attributes + SCIM throttling for SOW/contract

Hi Connor / Marissa,

Thanks again for yesterday's call. Procurement asked that we capture the remaining open items for the Statement of Work so they can circulate to legal. Two specific items we need clarified in writing before we move to a draft MOA:   

1) Federation / SSO attribute mapping — we need a clear mapping of what attributes Redwood will consume and which attributes are required vs optional. We have a strict schema on our side and need to ensure email / unique_id alignment.

2) SCIM provisioning throttling and bulk sync — MediPharm will onboard ~25k accounts initially and expect weekly full syncs from our directory. We need guaranteed behaviour for bulk import, clear rate limits, and a plan for retries/backoff should SCIM endpoints hit throttles.

Can you provide a short, definitive statement on both so Procurement can include it in the contract? Also please attach any relevant sample config or policy language you recommend.

Thanks,
Sarah Bates
IT Identity Lead — MediPharm
--
MediPharm IT

Subject: Re: SSO attributes + SCIM throttling for SOW/contract

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear summary. Putting this on paper below and attaching a short matrix and SCIM rate-limit doc for legal. High level:

1) Federation / SSO attribute mapping- Required attributes: subject (OIDC sub) or eduPersonPrincipalName (for SAML), mail (primary email), displayName, and a corporate unique_id attribute (we can accept employeeNumber or a custom claim). Redwood requires at least one stable unique identifier (sub or employeeNumber). Optional attributes: givenName, sn, department, title, phone.

- Attribute validation: Redwood will validate primary identifier formats (email well-formed, UUID patterns) on first login and surface mismatches to the SSO admin console. We will not transform or normalize identifiers beyond basic case-normalization for email.

- Mapping contract language suggestion (one-line to include in SOW): "MediPharm will provide a persistent unique identifier for each user in SAML/OIDC assertions (e.g., sub or employeeNumber). Redwood will accept the identifier as presented and perform basic normalization for email addresses; any additional attribute transformation must be agreed in writing."

2) SCIM provisioning and throttling- Bulk onboarding: Redwood supports SCIM v2 bulk provisioning patterns and can accept staged CSV imports via a secure ingestion job for the initial 25k users to limit API pressure.

- Rate limits: default SCIM API limits are 600 requests per minute per tenant; for onboarding bursts we can apply a temporary elevated window (up to 2,400 r/min for a 4-hour provisioning window) under an agreed change control.

- Backoff & retries: Redwood returns standard HTTP 429 with Retry-After header. Our recommended client behaviour: exponential backoff with jitter (start 1s, max 120s). Server-side, Redwood will queue up to 5,000 operations for short-term backpressure handling; beyond that operations return 503 with details.

- SLA note for contract: we propose an "Provisioning Throttle and Onboarding" clause that guarantees the elevated onboarding window for an initial migration up to 72 hours post-cutover, with defined change-control for any additional elevated windows.

I've attached: federation_attribute_matrix.csv (mapping example) and redwood_scim_rate_limits.pdf (details and suggested contract text). Looping in Kim (security) for any compliance caveats.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Connor — this is very helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side before we send to legal:

- For the primary identifier we plan to provide employeeNumber as the canonical UUID. Can you confirm Redwood can accept employeeNumber as the canonical id for account linking even if email changes?

- For the elevated provisioning window: we need the exact process to request that elevated quota during migration and what signals you will provide to our onboarding team if queueing occurs (so we can present status to our stakeholders).

Thanks — Sarah
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Bates <sarah.bates@medipharm.com>, connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 31 May 2028 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SSO attributes + SCIM throttling for SOW/contract

Hi Sarah — quick answers from security/ops perspective:  

- employeeNumber as canonical id: confirmed. We will accept employeeNumber as the persistent identifier for account linking; mapping logic will use employeeNumber when present and unique. If multiple users present the same employeeNumber we will flag as conflict and halt automated linking.

- Elevated provisioning window process: request via Support Portal (we'll include an API-based onboarding trigger in the onboarding runbook). Once requested, Redwood will: 1) provision an elevated quota token tied to your tenant and time window, 2) provide a status endpoint that returns live metrics (queued ops, processed ops/min, estimated time remaining) and 3) publish webhook callbacks for critical failures.

We will include that exact flow in the MOA appendix. Security note: webhooks are delivered over TLS with mutual TLS option if you require client certs.

Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Sarah / Procurement team — attaching a short draft MOA excerpt that includes the attribute mapping clause and the provisioning throttle appendix. Highlights:  

- Clause A.2: MediPharm will provide employeeNumber as the canonical identifier; Redwood will not change or reassign employeeNumber.
- Appendix B: Onboarding quota — Redwood will enable a single elevated provisioning window up to 72 hours for initial migration (max allowance: 2,400 r/min). Request made via Support Portal with 48-hour lead for production windows; emergency exceptions handled by on-call.

Please review the attached draft_moa_redwood_medipharm.docx and confirm any changes — once you greenlight, legal/procurement can move to signature.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
